summary: Keepalive queue deadlock triggers upstream OOM chain and elevated 5xx for enterprise tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden spike in 5xx errors beginning ~2026-03-12T18:40Z affecting mixed streaming + embedding workload. API gateway returned 502/503 to many requests and several upstream runtimes experienced OOMs and GPU driver disconnects.

Impact:
- ~80% of requests from the customer's prod route failed with 502/503 for ~22 minutes.
- Real-time dashboards for the customer degraded; multiple user-facing failures observed.

Environment:
- prod | us-west
- Dedicated pool assigned to Nimbus Analytics
- Mixed workload: long-lived streaming sessions (chat) + large sparse embedding uploads

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer runs concurrent streaming sessions while performing a 20M-row embedding bulk upload.
2) Agent observed keepalive connection queue growth on API gateway and long socket hold times.
3) Upstream runtime workers hit file-descriptor exhaustion, then page faults and eventual nvml/gpu driver disconnects.
4) API gateway began returning 502s while runtimes restarted, producing elevated 5xx floor.

Observed logs (snippets):
- apigw: "accept_queue=32768 hold_time_ms=12000 conn_count=1024 keepalive_reaper=stalled"
- runtime: "OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
- runtime: "nvml: device lost"
- scheduler: "worker pid=4512 killed: out-of-memory (rss=27.3GB)"

Additional context:
- Customer is on a dedicated capacity plan and had pinning to a specific model variant.
- Rate-limiting headers were near default limits; customer traffic pattern included many small keepalive pings and a handful of very large embedding requests.

2026-03-12 18:55 - Lucas Moreno (SRE): Observed keepalive queue growth on apigw in us-west and FD errors in runtime logs. Marking as P0 and routing traffic to fallback pool for mitigation.
2026-03-12 19:05 - Support (CS): Notified customer of temporary routing to a warmed dedicated fallback and advised to pause bulk embedding upload.
2026-03-12 19:18 - Engineering: Deployed temporary throttling policy for large multipart embeddings and increased apigw accept queue sizing. Monitoring for stabilization.
2026-03-12 19:40 - Lucas Moreno: Error rate returned to baseline after throttling and routing change. Began post-incident data collection for RCA.
2026-03-13 09:12 - Priya Desai (Eng): Confirmed root cause and rolled a kernel-selection fallback to reduce nvml resets; created follow-up task INT-11522 for autoshed policy improvements.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: pure GPU driver instability due to long-lived heavy embedding writes. Logs showed nvml errors but were preceded by FD exhaustion.
Correlation found between keepalive pool saturation on apigw and runtime fd table growth; many sockets held open by streaming sessions and multipart embedding upload chunking.
Reproduction attempted in staging with synthetic mix: confirmed accept_queue growth under mixed workload and subsequent runtime worker OOM after fd exhaustion.
Observed that default throttler policy allowed embedding workers to open many concurrent file descriptors for chunked uploads — no upstream backpressure applied early enough.
Routing to warmed fallback pool (more permissive prewarm) reduced connection churn and prevented further driver disconnects while throttling addressed the root flow.
Postmortem trace linked to an older runtime kernel selection path that did lower fd reuse; patch PR #8421 adds a keepalive-friendly accept loop and reuses FDs more aggressively.
resolution:
Mitigations applied during incident:
- Temporarily routed Nimbus traffic to a warmed fallback dedicated pool to drain accept queue pressure.
- Applied an emergency throttling rule to limit concurrent multipart embedding connections from the tenant.
- Increased apigw accept queue and keepalive reaper frequency to reclaim stalled sockets faster.
Post-incident fixes:
- Merged runtime PR to improve FD reuse and accept-loop backpressure (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421).
- Rolled kernel-selection fallback to reduce nvml resets on similar mixed workloads.
- Created follow-ups: INT-11522 (autoshed/retry policy tuning), INT-11523 (observability: add FD/accept-queue alarms per-tenant), and a customer-facing guidance doc for recommended upload patterns.
Customer follow-up: Nimbus confirmed normal service and accepted a schedule for a post-incident retro on 2026-03-16.
postmortem_followups: INT-11522: autoshed and throttler policy revamp
DOC-420: customer guidance for embedding uploads and keepalive best-practices
resolution_status: Mitigated and patched; follow-up tasks open
